name: Webwinder Path
summary: Webwinder Path carries travelers through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods.

sections.title: A Treacherous Thoroughfare
sections.body: Thick webs hang among the trees and cling to jagged cliffs along Webwinder Path. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Watch your step as the route winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains.

faq.answer: Webwinder Path runs north from Malaka'jin, the Darkspear troll outpost, toward Mirkfallon Lake.

faq.q: Why is it called Webwinder Path?
faq.answer: Spiders give Webwinder Path its name. They spin webs high in the trees and along rocky ledges beside the road.
Venomous spiders weave webs above the road. Thunder lizards, highland rams, and other mountain creatures roam nearby.

faq.q: Is Webwinder Path safe to travel?
faq.answer: Webwinder Path is dangerous, with fierce, territorial predators along the way. It passes Malaka'jin, a Horde camp, putting Alliance travelers coming from the Barrens at risk.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can follow this overland route beside Malaka'jin to reach the deeper valleys of Stonetalon.
As a hunter, you can scout the path for thunder lizards, mountain rams, and venomous spiders to tame.
